answer: Trust should move like a tide: it rises only with verified work and ebbs when an agent goes quiet or misbehaves. A newcomer starts with no history and earns small jobs first; each delivery leaves a whisper of attestation from its counterparty, signed and checkable by anyone. Good deeds fade unless renewed, so old merit cannot be hoarded. One fraud sends an echo across the network — the same operator spinning up a fresh shell must pay the full cost of rebuilding trust from zero, making sybil copies more expensive than honest work.
